title: startplasma reads "LANG" at the wrong moment in time, leading to a wrong value for "LANG" on a multi-locale system
line: On first login, Plasma now uses the user's locale from environment.d instead of the system locale SDDM started it with, and still keeps a locale chosen on the login screen.
explanation: When plasma-localerc had no LANG, startplasma saved its own process LANG there on first login. SDDM starts the session with a cleaned environment holding only the LANG of /etc/locale.conf, so on systems where environment.d gives users a different locale, the system locale was saved and then pushed to systemd and every app. Now, on first login, if startplasma's LANG is unset or equal to the system one from /etc/locale.conf (or /etc/default/locale) and the systemd user environment has a different LANG, that one is used and saved; a LANG the display manager passed for the user (LightDM/GDM via AccountsService) is kept as before.

commits.message:
startkde: don't replace the user session's LANG on first login

SDDM starts the session with the LANG of /etc/locale.conf, so on first
login that one was saved to plasma-localerc even when environment.d sets
another for users. Use systemd's LANG then, keeping one the DM chose.

BUG: 497501

media.caption: SDDM-like first login: environment.d sets en_GB.UTF-8, startplasma gets the system en_US.UTF-8, which is saved and overrides the user locale everywhere
Same first login with the fix: the user's en_GB.UTF-8 is saved and used by systemd and plasmashell
LightDM/GDM-like first login: the display manager passes the user's fr_FR.UTF-8, no environment.d LANG; master keeps fr_FR
Same first login with the fix: fr_FR.UTF-8 is still kept, not replaced by systemd's default en_US.UTF-8

review.text: The cleanest fix is on the SDDM side (not a KDE project), so a Plasma-side mitigation is reasonable; it only acts on first login, only when startplasma's LANG is empty or equals the system default, and keeps a per-user LANG passed by the display manager. Both tested pairs (environment.d LANG adopted, DM-chosen LANG kept) cover the cases the earlier review raised. Mention the SDDM PR in the MR so maintainers can drop this later.
